authority_note: arcs-verify owns the C2PA independent-verification report and comparison contract. It does not own generic provenance-signal semantics (arcs-standard) and does not own the native observation receipt serialization (arcs-srs). Nothing here ratifies a C2PA conclusion; it fixes the vocabulary in which arcs-verify reports one.

aggregate_match_boolean.rationale: Ratified doctrine section 13 prohibits the word 'verified' without an axis in conforming verifier output. A single aggregate match Boolean also collapses causally distinct divergences: a certificate that aged out between observation and recomputation would report the same value as a substantive disagreement.

synthetic_absent_comparison.rule: When 'observed' is absent, 'comparison' MUST be absent. Emitting an array of not_evaluated comparisons in place of an absent comparison is prohibited: it manufactures the appearance of an evaluation that was never possible.
synthetic_absent_comparison.rationale: not_evaluated is a finding about an evaluation that was in scope. No comparison was in scope when there is nothing to compare against.

exit_status_semantics.rule: The semantic status of a native invocation MUST be determined from the machine report. Process exit status MUST NOT be used to decide valid versus invalid.
exit_status_semantics.evidence: The pinned native validator exits 0 for validation_state Valid AND for validation_state Invalid, and exits non-zero only when a required input is unavailable. Exit status separates 'could not evaluate' from 'evaluated'; it does not separate valid from invalid.

legacy_flattened_status.rule: Parsers MUST read the scoped 'validation_results' object (activeManifest / ingredientDeltas). The legacy top-level 'validation_status' array MUST NOT be used as the source of findings.
legacy_flattened_status.evidence: The legacy array is a flattened view in which active-manifest and ingredient findings collapse together with no scope marker, producing duplicate entries.

revocation_silence.rule: Revocation MUST be reported as not_evaluated under hermetic settings. Absence of a revocation failure MUST NOT be represented as non-revocation.
revocation_silence.evidence: Native revocation checking occurs only via OCSP, is default-off, requires network I/O, and offers no mechanism to inject captured OCSP responses for offline replay.

manifest_structure.description: Internal integrity of the manifest store: assertion hashed-URI bindings resolve and match.

asset_binding.description: Binding of the manifest to the asset bytes (hard binding / data hash).

claim_signature.description: Cryptographic validity of the claim signature over the claim, and whether the signature was made inside the signing certificate's validity window.

signer_trust.description: Whether the signing credential chains to trust material the caller supplied. This is a property of caller-supplied inputs, not of the asset.

signer_validity.description: Whether the signing certificate is within its validity window at the validation instant. Held separate from signer_trust: 'we do not trust this issuer' and 'this was fine and aged out' are different facts.
signer_validity.clock_mitigation: A trusted timestamp on the same manifest (timeStamp.trusted) anchors the validation instant and mitigates wall-clock drift for this axis. Without one, this axis is not reproducible across wall-clock passage.

timestamp.description: Presence, integrity, and trust of an RFC 3161 style trusted timestamp over the claim signature.

revocation.description: Revocation status of the signing credential.

ingredient.description: Findings scoped to ingredient manifests, carried in validation_results.ingredientDeltas. Inherits the reproducibility class of whichever codes actually appear.

axis_status_values.satisfied: The native validator produced a success finding for this axis and no failure finding.
axis_status_values.failed: The native validator produced at least one failure finding for this axis.
axis_status_values.indeterminate: The native validator produced only informational findings for this axis; it declined to resolve the axis either way.
axis_status_values.not_evaluated: The axis was in scope but the native validator produced no finding for it, or hermetic settings forced it out of evaluation.
axis_status_values.not_applicable: The axis cannot apply to this artifact class.

reproducibility_classes.byte_deterministic: Reproducible from the frozen input bytes alone.
reproducibility_classes.policy_dependent: Depends on caller-supplied policy material (trust anchors, allowed lists, EKU configuration). Reproducible only against a digest-identical policy basis.
reproducibility_classes.time_dependent: Depends on the validation instant. The pinned native validator exposes no validation-clock control, so this class is not caller-pinnable.
reproducibility_classes.resource_dependent: Depends on an external resource that cannot be frozen and replayed (network revocation responses).
reproducibility_classes.validator_version_dependent: Depends on the native validator build. Applied at report level, not per axis: any axis can flip on a validator version change.

comparison_states.match: Both sides resolved the axis and resolved it identically, on a comparable basis.
comparison_states.mismatch: Both sides resolved the axis on a comparable basis and resolved it differently.
comparison_states.not_comparable: The two sides were produced on bases that are not comparable for this axis; no divergence claim can be made either way.
comparison_states.not_evaluated: The comparison itself was not performed, because one side carries no finding for the axis.

comparison_reasons.same_inputs_same_semantics: Same frozen inputs, same validator identity and version, same policy basis, and a reproducibility class that permits substantive comparison.
comparison_reasons.validator_implementation_delta: The two sides were produced by different native implementations.
comparison_reasons.validator_version_delta: The two sides were produced by different versions of the same native implementation.
comparison_reasons.trust_basis_delta: The two sides used different trust material or trust mode.
comparison_reasons.revocation_basis_delta: The two sides used different revocation evidence or revocation posture.
comparison_reasons.timestamp_basis_delta: The two sides used different timestamp-authority trust material or timestamp posture.
comparison_reasons.validation_clock_delta: The two sides were evaluated at different validation instants, on an axis whose result depends on the validation instant, without a trusted timestamp to anchor it.
comparison_reasons.input_delta: The two sides were evaluated over different asset or manifest-store bytes.
comparison_reasons.policy_delta: The two sides applied different validator policy settings other than trust, revocation, or timestamp basis.
comparison_reasons.unsupported_native_feature: The axis exercises a native feature the pinned validator does not expose.
comparison_reasons.insufficient_evidence: The observation does not carry enough information to compare this axis.

integrity_postures.no_integrity_inference: This comparison supports no inference about the integrity or honesty of either side.
integrity_postures.possible_substantive_divergence: The two sides disagreed on a comparable basis, so a substantive disagreement is possible. This is a prompt to investigate, not a finding of tampering, bad faith, or falsity.
integrity_postures.not_assessable: Integrity cannot be assessed from this comparison at all.

reason_posture_matrix._note: Enforced by the bundle conformance checker, not by JSON Schema alone. Each entry maps a comparison state to the reasons legal in that state and, per reason, the single legal integrity posture.

comparability_predicates._note: Report-level facts the comparison engine consumes. Each is recomputed from the two sides' recorded inputs; none is accepted as an assertion.
comparability_predicates.validator_identity_match: Both sides name the same native implementation.
comparability_predicates.validator_version_match: Both sides name the same native implementation version.
comparability_predicates.asset_digest_match: Both sides record the same asset bytes digest.
comparability_predicates.manifest_store_digest_match: Both sides record the same manifest-store bytes digest.
comparability_predicates.trust_basis_match: Both sides record the same trust mode and the same trust-material digest.
comparability_predicates.settings_match: Both sides record the same applied validator settings digest.
comparability_predicates.validation_clock_comparable: Both sides evaluated at a comparable validation instant. False by default: the pinned validator exposes no validation-clock control, so this is true for a time_dependent axis only when a trusted timestamp anchors it.

hermeticity_facts._note: Facts arcs-verify can establish about its own invocation. Establishing them does NOT make a time_dependent axis reproducible: hermetic is not timeless.
hermeticity_facts.network_access_permitted: core.allowed_network_hosts was empty and no network-enabled option was set.
hermeticity_facts.remote_resource_fetch_attempted: verify.remote_manifest_fetch was false, so no remote manifest dereference was attempted.
hermeticity_facts.trust_list_uri_dereferenced: Trust material was supplied as local digest-pinned bytes; no trust-list URI was dereferenced.

manifest_acquisition_modes.embedded: Manifest store was embedded in the asset.
manifest_acquisition_modes.remote_reference: Asset referenced a remote manifest store; the referenced bytes were captured out of band and supplied locally.
manifest_acquisition_modes.external_supplied: Manifest store bytes were supplied as a separate file.
manifest_acquisition_modes.sidecar: Manifest store was supplied as a sidecar alongside the asset. UNEXERCISED by this contract's fixtures.
manifest_acquisition_modes.durable_recovery: Manifest store was recovered by soft binding. UNEXERCISED by this contract's fixtures.

unexercised_paths._note: Recorded deliberately. No input was manufactured to create coverage of these; a contract that claimed them would be claiming beyond its evidence.
features: a signer chaining to the official public C2PA trust list
